blockingReasons: Whether TPG Rise Climate, SK E&S and Deere still hold their disclosed Summit Carbon Holdings membership units at the cutoff date is not publicly resolved.
Current diluted ownership percentages, governance rights and several legal close dates are not publicly disclosed.
rationale: Summit Carbon Solutions remains a qualifying U.S. carbon-infrastructure development platform through Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III. TPG's $300 million investment came from the Rise Climate private-equity impact product and is out of scope for the infrastructure-manager census. The company is active but not operating after its 2026 route reset. Tiger and Summit Agricultural Group are current and Continental remained invested at year-end 2025, while the current status of Deere, SK E&S and TPG Rise Climate requires review before the full owner table can be applied.
recommendedChanges: Retain one Summit Carbon Solutions canonical record and treat Summit Carbon Holdings as its parent/alias rather than a duplicate.
Keep Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III as an active in-scope infrastructure owner from 2021 with a $100 million disclosed investment and no inferred percentage.
Record TPG Rise Climate's 2022 $300 million investment as an out-of-scope climate-private-equity period, not a TPG infrastructure holding.
Keep Summit Agricultural Group current and Continental current through its December 31, 2025 Form 10-K evidence; route Deere, SK E&S and TPG current status to review.

Describe Summit as an active development-stage platform, not an operating pipeline, and replace the stale five-state 2,000-mile and 20 Mtpa claims with the qualified 2026 Iowa-Nebraska-Wyoming route status.
Keep all capture, pipeline, storage and project LLCs subordinate to the single manager-level company.
